speaker: Jote
line_text: The barriers of the Wood are Her will given form, raised by our rites, suffused with Her spirit. These you shall never pass save with Lente's Tear. I have no more to say to you. Take with you she who has abandoned the Wood, and go. / Mjrn is yet in her spring. Trouble her no more. She would shake and scatter before the rough winds that blow beyond the Wood. / Seed is carried furthest on rough winds. Where it lands matters little, so long as it find fertile soil in which to take root.

speaker: Mjrn
line_text: An indescribable sensation overtook me within the mine. It reached out, closed about my heart... then all was darkness. This loathsome shadow...ageless and ancient beyond any viera or hume...what was it? / The will to quell my thoughts of the world outside the Wood...the courage to live beyond Her... Neither do I possess. Will I never share in the strength of my sisters?

speaker: Mjrn
line_text: Whence has this cockatrice come? These beasts, too, know loneliness... / Whence has this cockatrice come? These beasts, too, know loneliness... Is that a dewdrop pebble you have there? They are said to bring fortune to you on the day you find them. I remember gathering pebbles with my sister... (choices: Offer her your dewdrop pebbles. / Do nothing.) / Dewdrop pebbles are no common stones. They sometimes rain down with the afternoon showers or during thick morning fogs. They cannot be carried beyond the village, for they vanish. The pebbles can exist only here... not unlike the viera. / It is said dewdrop pebbles are crystals left when the vapors of the Wood mingle with the spirits of the trees. You can read the Wood's mood in their colors... as varied and as beautiful as the leaves. / The dewdrop pebbles fall in great number. It is not usual to find so many. And all of a common size. As though someone were...gathering them. / Thank you. I think this should be enough to help our visitor. / The dewdrop pebbles cannot survive outside the village. Should you leave, they will be lost. / It seems to show interest in dewdrop pebbles. Should you find some, will you bring them here? / This beast seems to show an interest in the pebbles. I thought I might show it more should I find any. Have you found any more? (choices: Offer her your dewdrop pebbles. / Do nothing.) / What brings this beast to us? Surely not only for the dewdrop pebbles has it come. / Have you found more of the pebbles? (choices: Offer her your dewdrop pebbles. / Do nothing.) / I believe its memory is lost. Looking on dewdrop pebbles seems to be of some help, though. It is close now to remembering, I can feel it. / I believe its memory is lost. Looking on the pebbles seems to be of some help, though. It is close now to remembering, I can feel it. You have found more of the pebbles? (choices: Offer her your dewdrop pebbles. / Do nothing.) / So long was she here, I had begun to grow fond of her. I am sorry to see her go. Sorry, and perhaps worried. Do you suppose she'll be all right? / So long was she here, I had begun to grow fond of her. I am sorry to see her go, but it is good she will be home again.

speaker: Chit; Cockatrice
line_text: (It stares intently at Mjrn.) / That viera bird won't stop starin'. She don't look very 'appy to me. Wonder wot's up wiv 'er? Nuffink serious, I 'ope. Mjrn, eh? Pretty name. Hmm...I 'ate seein' a fellow bird so mis'rable. Maybe I can do summink to cheer 'er up a bit? / (It seems to have an interest in the pebbles.) / Them sparkly pebbles ain't 'alf pretty, are they. Shame yer can't take 'em out the village. 'Ang about! 'Ow the 'eck do I know that? An' just 'ow many o' these blinkin' things do I need to fetch to cheer up Mjrn then, eh? / (It wears a doubtful expression.) / So many pebbles, jus' fallin' out the sky... See 'ow they sparkle... Reminds me o' summink... ...Aw, 'e'll love these, 'e will. 'Old on! Who'll love these? ...Wot the bleedin' 'ell am I on about? Get a grip, girl! / (It looks worried about something.) / Sparkle, sparkle... Once I get enough o' these sparkly pebbles together, I can go 'ome... 'Ang about! 'Ome! ...Blimey. If I got an 'ome, that'd mean I weren't always 'ere, wouldn't it? So where's me 'ome then? / (It seems to be...fidgeting.) / Sparkle, sparkle... I'm bloomin' sure I'm forgettin' summink...now wot the 'eck was it? Ooh, I'd forget me bleedin' beak if it weren't screw'd on! I'm gonna go crackers tryin'a remember... / A glowing object falls from under its wing!

speaker: Hala
line_text: Where Mjrn has gone is our concern, not yours. Interlopers are not welcome. A wind blows from beyond the Wood, stirring all it touches. I pray it does not disturb the peace of the village. / Mjrn went against the Green Word. The decision to welcome her back has met with much discord. These foreign winds bring much trouble for us. You may rest here if you like, but do not interfere with the doings of the village. / We choose this hidden place, secluded from the world beyond, to live as we have always lived. This is what it is to be viera. If you understand our ways even a little, you will not again set foot within our village.

speaker: Hala
line_text: We have heard the whisper of the Wood. It tells us to deny passage to the humes. So have we summoned the barriers in Golmore. Those to whom Jote gives her leave, who bear Lente's Tear, may pass—no other.

speaker: Hala
line_text: The vorpal bunnies of Golmore Jungle...their tail fur emits a subtle fragrance. It is essential in the making of vision dust. The preparation of vision dust is a trial for one who would be salve-maker. Once this is done, her apprenticeship is ended. / After I accepted Alja as an apprentice, the warder-chief came to me. She asked me to watch over her sister. And Nera...Nera can be meddlesome, but I know she means well. She is alone, at a distance...she watches our comings and goings with a clarity that those of us involved cannot.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: Ever has our elder led us down the right path. The laws she protects are absolute. If the Green Word forbids contact with the world outside, then so must it be. / There are those who have raised their voices against Mjrn's return, but I support the elder's decision. Never in the past has she erred. I do not think she is like to start now. / Always must Jote remain with the village, her thoughts on us and the Wood. She is our leader, our guide. Some think her too severe, yet the path the viera walk is long. Missteps early on, however slight, can lead us far astray.

trigger: requested by イベント管理.ヨーテ前半_再生
speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: To be viera is to abide by the Green Word. It is only natural that Jote's will and the will of the village be as one. If the Green Word forbids contact with the world outside, then so must it be.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: How have you breached our borders, interloper? Do the wood-warders slumber at their posts? / Even should you find Mjrn, to us she is forever lost. Once a viera has forsaken the Wood, return is forbidden. Besides, I would not think a hume's dull senses able to find her. You will be lucky if your flesh does not soon feed the feybeasts. / One who has left the Wood but once ought never be allowed to return. It is only natural that the children of the Wood should not traffic with the world beyond. It is our way. The elder is too forgiving of her sister. / When will you learn your trespass here is not welcome? Do not think all Ivalice yours to wander as you please.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: Leave me be. / Are you lost? Or do you trespass here willingly? Either way, the presence of humes disrupts the harmony of our village...you must realize this. / Once more the village is quiet, still. All reason for your presence is now gone, is it not? / Do you still not see? There is nothing here for you. Here we live out our time. Your time and ours are not meant to cross. So has it ever been, and so shall it ever be.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: The fane of the village elder is just beyond this bridge. What errand could a hume possibly have with her? / The salve-makers of our village gather at this house. A salve-maker must have knowledge not only of herbs, but of the Wood as a whole. With our knowledge of medicine and our healing hymns do we support and sustain the village as our elder, Jote, bids us. / Jote leads with Hala ever at her side. Hala herself is a salve-maker of great renown who has served the village as long as the village has stood. / The reagents we gather in the Wood—plant seeds and roots, tree sap, animal eggs, feathers—all are stored in the house behind me. The Wood is the world to us, and the world the Wood. As we are part of the Wood, so are we part of the world. In this is there balance, and bliss.

speaker: Alja
line_text: It is Mjrn you seek? She is usually just beyond this bridge, but I tell you now, you search in vain. I should not think she would even know who you are. / Golmore Jungle has blessed us with a new herb, and we must decide how best it might be used to enrich our medicines. It is a matter beyond your understanding. I would thank you to interrupt us no further. / We discuss the effect different methods of storage have on herbal potency. Do matters so beyond your grasp nonetheless hold interest for you? / Would you know more of the Wood? The life that burgeons in Her must be shown the proper respect. Beauty seldom comes without danger. To one who walks in ignorance, the Wood can seem dark, Her life promising naught but death.

speaker: Alja
line_text: A vorpal bunny? The vorpal bunnies come to Golmore Jungle every seven years. They favor an area south of the Needlebreak, I think. Why ask such a thing, I wonder... / I will honor my promise to Nera. You need not worry over me. Would you know how these things have come to pass? I was still a wood-warder new made, but my sister Rael wished to see me excel. This is why she charged me with the salve-maker's escort. I thought this burden too great, but as the sister of the warder-chief, expectations for me were high... My injury weighed heavy on my sister, but I did not want to leave her side. I sought Hala, leader of the salve-makers, for guidance. She heard my words, and opened for me the path of the salve-maker. / My decision is made. I will tell my sister that I have prepared the vision dust and been accepted as a salve-maker. We have not talked for many years. I only hope she will forgive me...

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: The sunward path leads to the fane of our elder, Jote. Though I cannot think she would speak with a hume. / You flaunt our laws, abandon our village...does returning here not shame you? Did you think a mere fifty years would find you forgiven? / The sunward path leads to the fane of our elder, Jote. She is here, though I cannot think she would speak with a hume. / Our houses bear little likeness to those of humes. They are places where those of like calling, be they wood-warders or salve-makers, gather. / The wooden screens about the village interest you? If our village is attacked, we welcome our guests with arrows from behind these screens. It is a grave matter, never to be spoken of idly.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: You are unwelcome in the Wood. She will not suffer humes to walk Her verdant paths; Her barriers deny you. Leave now, whilst you may. / You are unwelcome in the Wood. She will not suffer humes to walk Her verdant paths; Her barriers deny you. Leave now, whilst you may. / Though the Wood may change through waxing days and waning hours, ever she remains the same. Pilgrim of the Wood, look beyond time's facade to find your true self, untouched by time's flow. / The Wood whispers with the winds of distant lands, bringing us tidings from afar. A tranquil heart and keen ear might learn much of the world beyond the Wood, never needing to forsake Her gentle bosom. / If in our reclusion we are forgotten, then that, too, is as it must be. As countless spirits and uncountable visions before, the viera will fade to eldritch shadow, an echo of the Wood's voice on the wind.

speaker: Wood-warder
line_text: You walk a hidden enclave of the viera known to outlanders as Eruyt Village. We wish no consort with others. Leave us. / You walk a hidden enclave of the viera known to outlanders as Eruyt Village. We wish no consort with others. Leave us. / You walk a hidden enclave of the viera known to outlanders as Eruyt Village. Already your coming disrupts the stillness of the Wood. Leave us. / Many of our sisters have we lost to the beguiling winds of the outside world. We must lose no more. Your coming holds no joy for us. / Visitors are not welcome in this place. Leave the Wood. Your way shall not be barred.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: Our laws forfend contact with the world outside. Here silence and solitude will be your companions. / Mjrn, you seek? You seek in vain. / We are different...what more need you know? Accept, but do not seek to understand. Accept not, and you will never understand. / This place is one of quiet contemplation. Your presence disturbs its tranquillity more than I would expect... Nera alone seems cheered, but she has always been...unique. Do not look for such welcome from others. / You persist in visiting us. I did not think our welcome so...inviting. What do you think to find here? Or do you think not at all? Is it this sluggish wit that gives you humes such resilience? Intriguing...

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: I have no words to speak to a hume. / Did our laws not exist, I would still not consort with a hume. / The one sister has left. What are we to expect of the other? / Viera who leave the village are viera no more. Shadow and illusion make for fleet quarry, but there is little joy in their capture. / Our paths are of our own choosing. Should two paths diverge, we might look back upon the time they were one, but never can they be untrod.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: It is because the spring remains apart that the flowers bloom. ...You would not understand. / The flower that blooms upon the water may take root upon the land, but is it then the same flower? / Our village is like the spring, rising and falling among the branches of the Wood. Water that stands overlong may grow stagnant, but better this than it be clouded by waters coursed through foreign soils. / The flower that blooms upon the water, the flower that blooms upon the land. How are they alike? How do they differ? Are they really different at all? Or does the difference lie in how we perceive them? It vexes me. / At what do I look? I would know this answer myself. Water is like the soul: ever-changing, constant only in its inconstancy. It flows, and freezes. It joins the air, and rains down upon the Wood.

speaker: Wood-dweller
line_text: That light, what is it? A stone? (choices: Ask her to get it for you. / Do nothing.)

speaker: Nera
line_text: Mjrn? Why do you ask after her? I am not she. What is it you seek? / To show interest in the world outside is forbidden by our laws, but a mind once open to the unknown will not be denied. Is this not what has brought you to us? / To show interest in the world outside is forbidden by our laws, but a mind once open to the unknown will not be denied. Is this not what has brought you to us? / In truth I should not speak with you. But it is all right. The others do not concern themselves with my doings. Here was I born, and here I live. I do not think, though, that past and present need dictate the future. / The Green Word, the laws of our village, a future filled with ruin...if we dwell on such weighty matters, we are like to collapse under the burden. There is no end that is not also a beginning. The sun will rise and fall as it always has...this is enough for me.

speaker: Nera
line_text: You come because of the bill I posted? Then you will hear me tell of the vorpal bunny? (choices: I'm listening. / No, I don't think so.) / Thank you. Then I shall begin. The vorpal bunny is a black dreamhare that appears only once each seven years. The tail of this hare is a component vital in the making of vision dust, an incense said to fill the minds of those who breathe it with illusion. For a viera salve-maker, the preparation of vision dust is a rite of passage, one that Alja has yet to fulfil. Ever she remains an apprentice. Experience and skill she has, but the vorpal bunny eludes her capture—it is too quick. But for a lame leg, Alja would be salve-maker even now. They would chasten me for looking without for aid, but the tension between wood-warder and salve-maker of late leaves me little choice. Turn to you I must, but speak of this to no one. If the elders knew of the petition, they might guess at my involvement. / It is custom for an escort of wood-warders to accompany a salve-maker on her hunt of the dreamhare. But Alja cannot ask the wood-warders for aid, not now. It will be seven years before she has this chance again...must she wait so long? Find the vorpal bunny, and she need not. It is somewhere in Golmore Jungle. I shall await your return at the entrance to the village. / Your games do not amuse. / Alja was once wood-warder, but an accident left her unable to wield blade or bow. She now strives to become salve-maker. I would see her finish her apprenticeship, but her lame leg keeps her from hunting the vorpal bunny. Must she wait seven more years? Find the vorpal bunny, and she need not. It is somewhere in Golmore Jungle. I shall await your return at the entrance to the village. / Each viera takes an apprentice to guide and instruct. The bond they share is strong, and not always untroubled. Vexing, is it not? In my solitude I am free of such burdens. I sometimes count myself...lucky. Thank you for coming to my aid.

speaker: Rael
line_text: What errand have you with Mjrn? What errand could you have? You should leave before aught ill comes to pass. For your sake, and our own. / You have spoken with Jote. The wood-warders brook no trespass within the village. Leave now, and do not look back. / What errand brings you to our secluded wood? What concern of yours is Mjrn's flight? You should leave before aught ill comes to pass. For your sake, and our own. / We have known of the humes in the magicite mines. They fear us, and have not disturbed the Wood. We keep watch on them, but we do not interfere. Mjrn knew of this, but this was not enough for her. She left the Wood. / There are those who blame Jote for the deeds of her sisters. As elder, she must always defend the village. Until now, diligently she has. But she is not alone. We wood-warders stand at her side. Together we defend the Wood.

Ever do the storm clouds follow her...but why? / I would join my fellow warriors, but apprentices are not permitted outside the village. It is a hardship for me. What has become of Mjrn...? / I would join my fellow warriors, but apprentices are not permitted outside the village. It is a hardship for me. What has become of Mjrn...? / Mjrn has returned, but still a weight presses upon my heart. Why is this so? Is she...different, somehow? Is there something I might do to help her? / Betrayal begins with but a thought of the world beyond the Wood. This is why we fear its call. What found Mjrn in that beyond? Please, visit us no more. For Mjrn's sake, if no other.

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, ネフィーリア２４Ｔ.talk_vorpal_bunny
speaker: Rena
line_text: Once, warder-chief Rael's blood sister walked here. I saw her stride the Wood, loose arrows at quarry, and knew that I must be wood-warder. Now she walks the path of salve-maker, and I see her but seldom. Would that that accident had never happened. / I pray Alja becomes salve-maker soon. And I must work at becoming wood-warder. The wood-warders and salve-makers must work side by side with the elder. Perhaps now we are closer to this. I thank you, my friend unseen.

speaker: Rena
line_text: Can you feel it? This vileness on the wind, dulling the senses... I would have you vanquish this wild malboro. (choices: Accept / Decline) / Deep in Golmore Jungle, a wild malboro is come to the Mist-shrouded trails of the Feywood. Viera are keen of sense...the wild malboro is a natural foe to us. Even now the winds carry the stench of one such through the Wood. The scouts we have sent return overcome with its foulness. Kjrs, of our wood-warders second only to Rael, left to destroy this abomination, yet returned as the others, her senses stricken by the filth. We had thought them long extinct, but before the beast claimed her sight, Kjrs confirmed our fears: we faced a wild malboro. We suspect this creature survived within the Feywood, held in check by the fell bloom Rafflesia. With Rafflesia's defeat, it ranges now far abroad. Still the wood-warders would not look without for aid, but we cannot long ignore the threat to Wood and village. Even in such circumstance, an apprentice may not leave the village, much to my frustration. But you can go where I might not. Make for the Feywood. Fell the wild malboro. / That I seek your aid is shame enough. Please, be not so quick to spurn my plea. / The wild malboro is the sire of the common variety. The beast troubling us is like to have grown bold after Rafflesia fell. Viera are keen of sense...the breath the wild malboro spews forth is too much for us. You must journey to the Feywood and defeat it for us. / The stench drifting from the Feywood is no more. You have rid us of the wild malboro, have you not? Those taken ill have begun to recover. You have earned your bounty with honor. Take it. It comes from Rael herself. / Rael learned of my call to the world outside for aid. I had thought she would upbraid me for my misdeed, but she bade me bring you that reward instead. Go now, with her thanks, and my own. / Our business is done. Go now, with our thanks, outlander. May your path always be clear.

speaker: Wood-warder
line_text: This path leads to the cove of the wood-warders. You will find naught there for a hume. / This path leads to the cove of the wood-warders. You will find naught there for a hume. / The wood-warders dwell in the cove ahead. The doors of our house alone stand ever open, that we may fly swiftly to those in need of aid. Interlopers are not welcome. At your own peril do you tread. / With Jote's trust and blessing does Rael lead the house of the wood-warders. Our task of defending Wood and village is no small one. See that you do not disturb us. / The Green Word before all other things must we protect. In this we cannot look to others for aid.

line_text: Fran We will need Mjrn's help if we are to pass through the barriers of the Wood. She will know that I have come. Bring her to me. I will wait here for your return. / Fran I would avoid unnecessary...confrontation. Do what you must, and let us be off. When you are ready, we should return to Ozmone Plain in the west. The Henne Mines are then only a short distance south. / Fran With Lente's Tear we can pass the barriers of Golmore Jungle. The Gran Kiltias on Bur-Omisace waits beyond. Our business here is done. / Fran I would avoid unwanted confrontation. I shall wait for you here. My presence would only disquiet Mjrn. When I turned from the viera, I turned from my past. Too far is it now to turn back. / Fran The time given viera is long. Carefully must Mjrn consider her choice, for herself decide whether she will remain. She may choose the same path Jote walks, but it is her choice to make. Strength it takes to live by viera laws. Strength I may have lacked...

Kupo? I thought you looked familiar. You are the one who helped us on the Leviathan! We've had quite a time reaching this village. Oh, I hope you don't think we followed you here, kupo. That wouldn't do at all. Well, would you like to see my wares? You won't find many shops around here, kupo. Best stock up while you can! / Kupo? You don't look like any viera I've ever seen, kupo. Me, kupo? I am but a humble traveling merchant. As luck would have it, I happen to be traveling here! Would you like to see my wares? I'll warn you, though. I only sell to one kind of customer: the paying kind, kupo! / Any merchant worth his salt needs but one thing to do business: a customer, kupo!

Looking for something, kupo? / A little chilly inside the village... I've decided to set up shop out here, instead, kupo. Want to hear something scary, kupo? I have it on good authority there are monsters which mimic crystals, and pounce when you touch them! / I spoke with the viera elder about running my shop here. I was a little frightened at first, but she seems reasonable enough, kupo. Speaking of frightening, I have it on good authority that there are monsters which mimic crystals, and pounce when you touch them! / It feels as though time stands still here, but when I go into town to restock my wares...how much has happened while I've been away, kupo! Want to hear something scary, kupo? I have it on good authority there are monsters which mimic crystals, and pounce when you touch them!

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, ０２ルルチェ.talk_地図屋
speaker: Lulucce
line_text: Kupo! Where have I seen you before...? No matter...I know why you've come! I've just the thing to help you get to the bottom of all those viera secrets... / Kupo! Not a word from you, kupo. I know why you've come! I've just the thing to help you get to the bottom of all those viera secrets...

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, ０２ルルチェ.talk_地図屋
speaker: Lulucce
line_text: Would you like to buy a map, kupo? / What a shame, kupo! You already own all of the maps I have for sale. / Select a map to purchase: (choices: [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / [value][value] / Cancel) / So long, kupo! / Kupo! You don't have enough gil! Sorry, no gil, no map! / A fine purchase, kupo! You won't regret it. Moogle's honor! / Your location map for this area is complete!

speaker: Lulucce
line_text: There are barriers along the paths of Golmore Jungle, kupo. As though the jungle itself chooses who may pass, and who may not. I'm pure as the driven snow...but I still couldn't get through. Maybe the jungle doesn't like snow... Perhaps I'll ask one of these viera about it. / Before we came here, we were locked away in a cramped little cell, the sound of machinery clinking and clanking, kupo. But here...it's so quiet! I can finally hear myself think. Kupo-po-po... / A viera left the village not long ago. You would not believe how many things she bought before going! Kupo! Something tells me we won't be seeing her back this way again, kupo... I'm not sure why, but it makes me sad. You'll come back again...won't you?

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, ０２ルルチェ.talk_地図屋
speaker: Lulucce
line_text: One of the viera asked me to deliver something to the city, kupo. It was good to be part of the world again. Time seems to stand still here, kupo.

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, ０２ルルチェ.talk_地図屋
speaker: Lulucce
line_text: The viera sent me on an errand to town. There's trouble in the village, though of what manner I'm not quite sure. But they do need help, kupo! I think I can sense it, too, kupo. If I face just... so...I get a terrible tickle all through my nose! Ku...ku...KUPO! / Why, my nose doesn't tickle in the least! Always be thankful for small favors, kupo.

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, ０２ルルチェ.talk_地図屋
speaker: Lulucce
line_text: There was a commotion not long ago. Something fell from one of the trees. I get dizzy just thinking about it, kupo. I saw the wood-warders helping what looked to me like a cockatrice. Yes, definitely a cockatrice, kupo.

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, ０２ルルチェ.talk_地図屋
speaker: Lulucce
line_text: A cockatrice just darted past at tremendous speed, kupo. If it's not careful, it's like to have another spill, kupo. Oh, bother.
Hey, Mjrn lives here, doesn't she? We're here to see her.
You will leave at once.
It is not allowed for humes to walk on these grounds.
We'll go as soon as we've seen Mjrn.
If you can find her.
We're not leaving until you let us see her.
Fine then. We'll look for her ourselves.
I've heard the voice of the Wood. She says Mjrn is not in the village.
Jote. Where has she gone?
Why do you ask?
The Wood tells us where she has gone. Or...can you not hear Her?
You cannot. / Your ears are dull from hearing their harsh speech, I think.
Viera who have abandoned the Wood are viera no longer. / Mjrn, too, has left Her embrace.
And you forsake them in turn?
It is the will of the village. / Viera must live always with the Wood.
So is the Green Word, and so is our law.
We'll let you worry about keeping your laws.
Just do us a favor and stay out of our way. We'll find her ourselves.
Our sister has left the Wood and gone west.
She wanders warrens among men who hide themselves in clothes of cold iron.
Thus to me has the Wood spoken.
The viera may begin as part of the Wood, but the Wood is not the only end we may choose.
The same words I heard 50 years ago.

trigger: requested by カット.カット５
line_text: I heard the Wood's whispers.

trigger: requested by カット.カット６
line_text: Take it.

trigger: requested by カット.カット７
line_text: Lente's Tear is a permission. / Pass through the Wood and leave. To other places go. / That cannot be all!

trigger: requested by カット.カット８
line_text: I saw it when I left the village! Ivalice is changing! / How can the viera stand and do nothing at all?

trigger: requested by カット.カット９
line_text: Ivalice is for the humes. / The Wood alone is for us.

trigger: requested by カット.カット１０
line_text: But that is wrong! / How can we just hide here in the trees when all the world outside is on the move! / I, too, wish to live freely— to leave this Wood!

trigger: requested by カット.カット１１
line_text: Do not do this. / You must remain away from the humes. / Stay with the Wood. Live together with the Wood. / This is your way.

trigger: requested by カット.カット１２
line_text: But Fran—my sister! / I am no longer of you.

trigger: requested by カット.カット１３
line_text: I have discarded Wood and village. / I won my freedom. Yet my past has been cut away forever.

trigger: requested by カット.カット１１３
line_text: No longer can my ears hear the Green Word.

trigger: requested by カット.カット１４
line_text: This...solitude, you want, Mjrn? / Sister—

trigger: requested by カット.カット１５
line_text: No, Mjrn. Only one sister remains to you now. / You must forget my existence.

trigger: requested by カット.カット１７
line_text: I am sorry to make you do this. / She goes against the laws of the Wood. / I threw down these laws. It is better that I do this. / Better I than one who must uphold these laws herself.

trigger: requested by カット.カット１９
line_text: I have a request:

trigger: requested by カット.カット２０
line_text: Listen to the Wood's voice for me. / I fear— I fear She hates.

trigger: requested by カット.カット２２
line_text: The Wood longs for you. For the child gone from under Her boughs.

trigger: requested by カット.カット２３
line_text: A pleasant lie, that.

trigger: requested by カット.カット２４
line_text: Be cautious. / The Wood is jealous of the humes who have taken you. / I am as them, now. / Am I not?

trigger: requested by カット.カット２５
line_text: Good-bye, sister.
